papers.title: Retrofitting of a High-Performance Aerospace Component via Topology Optimization and Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: This research presents a novel methodology for lightweighting and cost reduction of components with high structural demands by integrating advanced design and manufacturing techniques. Specifically, it combines topology optimization (TO) with additive manufacturing (AM), also known as 3D printing. Unlike conventional approaches, the proposed method first determines the optimal geometry using an artificially stiff material, and only then evaluates real materials for structural and manufacturing feasibility. This design-first, material-second strategy enables broader material screening and maximizes weight reduction without compromising performance. The proposed workflow is applied to the design of a turbofan air intake—an aeronautical component operating under supersonic conditions—addressing both structural integrity and manufacturing feasibility. Three materials from distinct classes are assessed: two metallic alloys (aluminum alloy 6061 and titanium alloy, Ti6Al4V) and a high-performance polymer (polyetheretherketone, PEEK). This last option is preliminarily discarded after being analyzed for this specific application. Finite element (FE) simulations are used to evaluate the mechanical behavior of the optimized geometries, including bird-strike conditions. Among the evaluated manufacturing techniques, Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is identified as the most suitable for the metallic materials selected, providing an effective balance between performance, manufacturability, and aerospace compliance. This study illustrates the potential of TO–AM synergy as a sustainable and efficient design approach for next-generation aerospace components. Simulation results demonstrate a weight reduction of up to 71% while preserving critical functional regions and maintaining structural integrity in Al 6061 and Ti6Al4V cases, under the diverse loading conditions typical of real flight scenarios, while PEEK remains an attractive option for uses where mechanical demands are less stringent.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于拓扑优化与增材制造结合的航空部件轻量化设计，虽然使用了Ti6Al4V，但并未深入探讨其力学性能或疲劳特性，因此与用户关注的Ti-6Al-4V基础力学与疲劳研究方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on a design methodology (topology optimization) and component-level simulation rather than on mechanical property characterization or fatigue performance of Ti-6Al-4V; no experimental mechanical testing or fatigue data are provided.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过拓扑优化和增材制造实现航空部件轻量化和降成本。
summary_zh.method: 先设计最优几何再评估材料的'设计优先'策略，结合SLM和FE仿真。
summary_zh.result: 在Ti6Al4V和Al6061中实现71%减重，结构完整性保持。
summary_zh.validation: 有限元仿真模拟鸟撞等工况。

summary_en.motivation: Propose a design-first, material-second methodology combining topology optimization and additive manufacturing to lightweight and reduce cost of high-performance aerospace components.
summary_en.method: The optimal geometry is determined using an artificially stiff material, then real materials (Al 6061, Ti6Al4V, PEEK) are evaluated via FE simulations for structural and manufacturing feasibility; SLM is chosen for metallic options.
summary_en.result: Weight reduction of up to 71% is achieved for Ti6Al4V and Al 6061 while preserving critical functional regions and maintaining structural integrity under flight loads including bird-strike.
summary_en.validation: Finite element simulations of the optimized geometries under diverse loading conditions, including bird-strike.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Method for Determining Material Strength Based on Hardness Measurements: A Case Study of the Ti6Al4V Alloy
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of estimating the tensile strength of Ti6Al4V alloy, based on HV measurements. The investigation included samples that were manufactured using both additive technology and conventional methods, under various conditions: as-built, heat-treated, and untested mechanically. Static tensile tests and HV measurements were performed to assess the influence of the manufacturing method, heat treatment, and mechanical loading on material performance. The highest tensile strength was recorded for as-built samples, while the greatest ductility was observed in conventionally drawn bar samples. Hardness values generally correlated with tensile strength trends; however, in heat-treated specimens, the relationship between hardness and tensile strength was found to be nonlinear. Specimens that were not subjected to tensile testing exhibited higher HV values than their mechanically tested counterparts, indicating a potential effect of prior deformation on the local material condition. The results confirm that hardness testing can be a useful indirect method for estimating the tensile strength of Ti6Al4V, particularly in materials with controlled and uniform microstructures. For additively manufactured and heat-treated materials, however, the current empirical models may require adjustment or enhancement using advanced predictive approaches. The proposed indirect method offers an alternative to destructive testing, especially in the industrial quality control context for metal AM.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了热处理对Ti6Al4V合金拉伸强度与硬度关系的影响，为后处理控制提供了间接评估方法。
llm.why_not_core: 论文主要关注硬度估算拉伸强度的方法，而非直接揭示后处理对疲劳或力学性能的调控机理。

summary_zh.motivation: 评估通过硬度测量间接估算Ti6Al4V合金拉伸强度的可行性。
summary_zh.method: 对增材制造和传统方法制备的Ti6Al4V样品进行拉伸试验和HV硬度测量。
summary_zh.result: 硬度与拉伸强度总体相关，但热处理后样品呈现非线性关系，增材制造样品强度最高。
summary_zh.validation: 通过对比不同工艺状态下硬度与拉伸数据的实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: This study evaluates the feasibility of indirectly estimating the tensile strength of Ti6Al4V alloy from hardness measurements across different manufacturing routes and post-processing conditions.
summary_en.method: Static tensile tests and Vickers hardness measurements were performed on Ti6Al4V samples fabricated by additive manufacturing and conventional methods, including as-built and heat-treated conditions.
summary_en.result: Hardness generally correlated with tensile strength, but a nonlinear relationship was observed in heat-treated specimens; as-built samples exhibited the highest tensile strength.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation was achieved by comparing hardness data with tensile test results from multiple material conditions.
